Hybrid solutions such as integrating NOWPayments for crypto alongside a restricted platform like Gumroad give you partial control but still leave you dependent on third-party infrastructure. Base-layer stacks like COREMERCH's Edge Commerce Stack ($197) deploy self-owned architecture — Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and NOWPayments for crypto processing. How They Handle Restricted Countries

Platforms like Stripe and PayPal exclude entire countries based on geopolitical risk assessments, not individual merchant behavior. A PayPal account suspension can freeze your funds for up to 180 days with no appeal. Workarounds that rely on these platforms inherit their restrictions. Hybrid solutions reduce but don't eliminate dependency. Sovereign infrastructure stacks bypass these limitations entirely by using globally accessible tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare, and Supabase. Your commerce stack operates independently of any single platform's country policies.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Stripe and PayPal charge 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction but can withhold funds indefinitely in restricted countries. Crypto processors like NOWPayments charge 0.5% with no KYC and no buyer account required. Transactions on networks like BSC, Solana, or TRON cost under $0.10. Workarounds add hidden costs — currency conversion fees, local gateway charges, and the risk of fund freezes. Sovereign stacks have predictable costs: a one-time deployment fee for infrastructure you own forever, plus minimal transaction fees for crypto processing.
Stripe's exclusion of 149 countries isn't an oversight — it's a structural decision. Sovereign infrastructure is the permanent alternative.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Platforms like Gumroad or Lemon Squeezy own your customer data, product delivery logic, and payment processing. Workarounds give you partial control but still rely on rented infrastructure. Sovereign stacks give you full ownership of every component. Cloudflare Workers automate order processing, Supabase stores your data, and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 delivers your products. After deployment, COREMERCH has no access to your stack — you own it entirely, with no subscriptions or recurring fees.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you're selling one-off products and accept temporary access, a workaround might suffice. If you want partial control without building from scratch, a hybrid solution could work. If you're building a long-term digital business in a restricted country, sovereign infrastructure is the only permanent solution. COREMERCH's Edge Commerce Stack ($197) deploys a complete, self-owned stack in 48 hours, configured for your specific products and tested end-to-end. It's not a workaround — it's base-layer infrastructure designed for creators Stripe locked out.
